subject: released CPO mask_loss aggregation contract under ZeRO-3 versus ZeRO-2

published_claim.paper: arXiv:2607.04364, RL Forgets! Towards Continual Policy Optimization
published_claim.scope: The paper's headline concerns continual-retention/adaptation performance. The mask_loss aggregation issue audited here is an implementation/logging property, not a contradiction of the paper's published retention headline.

trainer.finding: In ZeRO-3, each rank adds only its partition's masked absolute deviation while dividing by the tensor's global masked-support count, then accelerator.gather(...).nanmean() is logged. In ZeRO-2/no-DeepSpeed, each rank computes the full tensor contribution and the same nanmean preserves it. The exact same trainer blob is still on public main at audit time.

launchers.gpu_scope: README states paper RL launchers are configured for eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs for 2B, 4B and 8B. The shell scripts themselves discover the number of visible GPUs rather than hard-failing on a different world size.

environment.readme_pins: Linux, NVIDIA H100, Python 3.12, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.8.0, flash-attn 2.8.3, deepspeed 0.16.4
environment.requirements_lock_strength: Most Python packages are version-pinned, including accelerate 1.11.0, transformers 4.57.3 and trl 0.27.0; one dependency is a git URL without an immutable commit pin, so this is strong but not a fully content-addressed environment lock.

clean_worker_source_equivalent_check.result: 0 mismatches for corrected sum versus full metric and 0 mismatches for released mean versus full/world_size at 1e-10; max corrected absolute error 5.684341886080802e-14.
clean_worker_source_equivalent_check.scope: Worker used torch 2.10.0+cpu and explicitly did not execute DeepSpeed.

auditor_independent_check.method: NumPy-only source-equivalent implementation; no worker-code import and no DeepSpeed

reproduction_evidence.formal_identity: For each tensor i with global protected support R_i and disjoint ZeRO-3 partitions P_r, summing rank partials sum_{j in R_i∩P_r}|theta-ref|/|R_i| over r exactly reconstructs the full masked-L1 term. Therefore the released rank mean is the full value divided by world size W, up to floating-point summation error.

independent_replication: The auditor check is an independent local code path, not a third-party external reproduction. No protocol-matched external issue/report was recovered; the public repository issue search returned no mask_loss issue at audit time.
failed_replication: None recovered for this logging property.
scope_and_corrections: The clean worker's core algebra is confirmed. Under an eight-rank ZeRO-3 run, the released logged mask_loss is on a 1/8 scale relative to the full masked-L1 definition; under ZeRO-2 replicated parameters, nanmean preserves the full scale.

Because the README states eight GPUs for all paper RL methods and the 2B launcher uses ZeRO-2 while 4B/8B use ZeRO-3, cross-scale TensorBoard mask_loss values are not numerically comparable without correcting aggregation, conditional on those documented eight-rank launch conditions and equal underlying metric/lambda.
The source comment calling the ZeRO-3 nanmean a consistent relative measure is defensible only within a fixed world size. It is not invariant across world size or ZeRO stage.
No historical TensorBoard event files were authenticated in this audit, so this does not prove what any particular archived run logged.
This is logging-only. It neither proves nor disproves the separate owner-only regularizer-gradient scaling issue and does not by itself change training behavior.
blocker: No pinned Python 3.12 + torch 2.8.0 + DeepSpeed 0.16.4 multi-GPU execution or historical TensorBoard event bundle was available in this audit environment.
reopen_on: Upstream logging fix/release, pinned multi-GPU DeepSpeed reproduction, authenticated historical TensorBoard files, or a matched external report. Keep gradient-scaling experiments as a separate axis.
